chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Salama ibn al-Khattab, from Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Ali ibn Ribat, from Ubayd Allah ibn Salih, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:
I said to him, 'A woman performing Tamattu' performs Tawaf, then menstruates?' He said: 'She performs Sa'i between As-Safa and Al-Marwa, and she fulfills her Tamattu'.'

key_terms.تَسْعَى: She performs Sa'i (walking between Safa and Marwa)
key_terms.تَطُوفُ: She performs Tawaf (circumambulation of the Kaaba)
key_terms.مُتَمَتِّعَةٌ: A woman performing Hajj al-Tamattu' (combining Umrah and Hajj)

ai.seo_question: What must a woman do if she menstruates after Tawaf but before Sa'i during Hajj al-Tamattu'?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that a woman performing Hajj al-Tamattu' who menstruates after completing Tawaf but before Sa'i is not exempted from the latter; she must perform Sa'i to complete her Umrah. This ruling highlights the distinct nature of Sa'i as an independent pillar (rukn) within the Umrah rituals, separate from the state of ritual purity required for Tawaf. It underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that menstruation does not invalidate the already-performed Tawaf nor the obligation of Sa'i, ensuring the completeness of the Umrah component before proceeding to Hajj.
